arxiv-1608-04954.title: Measurement of the underlying-event properties with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-1608-04954.creator: Yuri Kulchitsky[1ex] on behalf of the ATLAS collaboration, [3mm] Institute of Physics, National Academy of Sciences, Minsk, Belarus
arxiv-1608-04954.description: Abstract A correct modelling of the underlying event in proton-proton collisions is important for the proper simulation of kinematic distributions of high-energy collisions. The ATLAS collaboration extended previous studies at 7 TeV with a leading track or jet or Z boson by a new study of Drell-Yan events in 1.

arxiv-2204-02966.title: Gauge Quantum Thermodynamics of Time-local non-Markovian Evolutions
arxiv-2204-02966.creator: Fernando Nicacio, Raphael N. P. Maia
arxiv-2204-02966.description: Abstract Dealing with a generic time-local non-Markovian master equation, we define current and power to be process-dependent as in classical thermodynamics. Each process is characterized by a symmetry transformation, a gauge of the master equation, and is associated with different amounts of heat and/or work.

arxiv-2212-14542.title: Recurrent Problems in the LOCAL Model
arxiv-2212-14542.creator: Akanksha Agrawal, John Augustine, David Peleg, Srikkanth Ramachandran
arxiv-2212-14542.description: Abstract The paper considers the SUPPORTED model of distributed computing introduced by Schmid and Suomela [HotSDN’13], generalizing the LOCAL and CONGEST models. In this framework, multiple instances of the same problem, differing from each other by the subnetwork to which they apply, recur over time, and need to be solved efficiently online.

arxiv-2402-03929.title: Viscous regularization of the MHD equations Thanks: Submitted to the editors August 7, 2026.
arxiv-2402-03929.creator: Tuan Anh Dao, Lukas Lundgren, Murtazo Nazarov
arxiv-2402-03929.description: Abstract Nonlinear conservation laws such as the system of ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations may develop singularities over time. In these situations, viscous regularization is a common approach to regain regularity of the solution. In this paper, we present a new viscous flux to regularize the MHD equations which holds many attractive properties.

arxiv-2404-12763.title: The Length and the Width of the Human Brain Circuit Connections are Strongly Correlated
arxiv-2404-12763.creator: Dániel Hegedűs, Vince Grolmusz
arxiv-2404-12763.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Dániel Hegedűs, Vince Grolmusz. The correlations of several fundamental properties of human brain connections are investigated in a consensus connectome, constructed from 1064 braingraphs, each on 1015 vertices, corresponding to 1015 anatomical brain areas. The properties examined include the edge length, the fiber number, or edge width, meaning the number of discovered axon bundles forming the edge and the occurrence number of the edge, meaning the number of individual braingraphs where the edge exists.

arxiv-2404-15296.title: Maximum Discrepancy Generative Regularization and Non-Negative Matrix Factorization for Single Channel Source Separation
arxiv-2404-15296.creator: Martin Ludvigsen and Markus Grasmair
arxiv-2404-15296.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Martin Ludvigsen and Markus Grasmair. The idea of adversarial learning of regularization functionals has recently been introduced in the wider context of inverse problems. The intuition behind this method is the realization that it is not only necessary to learn the basic features that make up a class of signals one wants to represent, but also, or even more so, which features to avoid in the representation.

arxiv-2407-08020.title: Interactive Segmentation Model for Placenta Segmentation from 3D Ultrasound images
arxiv-2407-08020.creator: Hao Li, Baris Oguz, Gabriel Arenas, Xing Yao, Jiacheng Wang, Alison Pouch, Brett Byram, Nadav Schwartz, Ipek Oguz
arxiv-2407-08020.description: Abstract Placenta volume measurement from 3D ultrasound images is critical for predicting pregnancy outcomes, and manual annotation is the gold standard. However, such manual annotation is expensive and time consuming. Automated segmentation algorithms can often successfully segment the placenta, but these methods may not consistently produce robust segmentations suitable for practical use.

arxiv-2407-12122.title: Observable and ionizing properties of star-forming galaxies with very massive stars and different initial mass functions
arxiv-2407-12122.creator: D. Schaerer, J. Guibert, R. Marques-Chaves, F. Martins
arxiv-2407-12122.description: Abstract Context. The presence of very massive stars (VMS) with masses > 100 >100 M ⊙ is now firmly established in the Local Group, nearby galaxies, and out to cosmological distances. If present, these stars could boost the UV luminosity and ionizing photon production of galaxies, helping to alleviate the overabundance of UV-bright galaxies found with JWST at high redshift.

arxiv-2407-17473.title: Improving engagement, diversity, and retention in computer science with RadGrad: Results of a case study CCS: Social and professional topics Informal education CCS: Social and professional topics Computing literacy
arxiv-2407-17473.creator: Philip M. Johnson, Carleton Moore, Peter Leong, Seungoh Paek
arxiv-2407-17473.description: Abstract . Objectives RadGrad is a curriculum initiative implemented via an application that combines features of social networks, degree planners, individual learning plans, and serious games. RadGrad redefines traditional meanings of “progress” and “success” in the undergraduate computer science degree program in an attempt to improve engagement, retention, and diversity.

arxiv-2504-15671.title: On the approximation of the Riemannian barycenter
arxiv-2504-15671.creator: Simon Mataigne, P.-A. Absil, Nina Miolane
arxiv-2504-15671.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Simon Mataigne, P.-A. Absil, Nina Miolane. We present a method for computing an approximate Riemannian barycenter of a collection of points lying on a Riemannian manifold. Our approach relies on the use of theoretically proven under- and over-approximations of the Riemannian distance function. We compare it to Riemannian steepest descent on the exact objective function of the Riemannian barycenter and to an approach that approximates the Riemannian logarithm using lifting maps. Experiments are conducted on the Stiefel manifold.

arxiv-2511-10821.title: MECHBench: A Set of Black-Box Optimization Benchmarks originated from Structural Mechanics
arxiv-2511-10821.creator: Iván Olarte Rodríguez, Maria Laura Santoni, Fabian Duddeck, Carola Doerr, Thomas Bäck, Elena Raponi
arxiv-2511-10821.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Iván Olarte Rodríguez, Maria Laura Santoni, Fabian Duddeck, Carola Doerr, Thomas Bäck, Elena Raponi. Benchmarking is essential for developing and evaluating black-box optimization algorithms, providing a structured means to analyze their search behavior. Its effectiveness relies on carefully selected problem sets used for evaluation.

arxiv-2512-02797.title: Gain-Scheduling Data-Enabled Predictive Control for Nonlinear Systems with Linearized Operating Regions Code available: https://github.com/SebsDevLab/GS_DeePC.git
arxiv-2512-02797.creator: Sebastian Zieglmeier, Mathias Hudoba de Badyn, Narada D. Warakagoda, Thomas R. Krogstad, Paal Engelstad
arxiv-2512-02797.description: Abstract This paper presents a Gain-Scheduled Data-Enabled Predictive Control (GS-DeePC) framework for nonlinear systems based on multiple locally linear data representations. Instead of relying on a single global Hankel matrix, the operating range of a measurable scheduling variable is partitioned into regions, and regional Hankel matrices are constructed from persistently exciting data.

arxiv-2512-12468.title: Autonomously Unweaving Multiple Cables Using Visual Feedback
arxiv-2512-12468.creator: Tina Tian, Xinyu Wang, Andrew L. Orekhov, Fujun Ruan, Lu Li, Oliver Kroemer, Howie Choset
arxiv-2512-12468.description: Abstract Many cable management tasks involve separating out the different cables and removing tangles. Automating this task is challenging because cables are deformable and can have combinations of knots and multiple interwoven segments. Prior works have focused on untying knots in one cable, which is one subtask of cable management.

arxiv-2601-23139.title: Automated Testing of Prevalent 3D User Interactions in Virtual Reality Applications
arxiv-2601-23139.creator: Ruizhen Gu, José Miguel Rojas, Donghwan Shin
arxiv-2601-23139.description: Abstract Virtual Reality (VR) technologies offer immersive user experiences across various domains, but present unique testing challenges compared to traditional software. Existing VR testing approaches enable scene navigation and interaction activation, but lack the ability to automatically synthesise realistic 3D user inputs (e.g, grab and trigger actions via hand-held controllers).

arxiv-2602-23266.title: Discourse-Aware Dual-Track Streaming Response for Low-Latency Spoken Dialogue Systems
arxiv-2602-23266.creator: Siyuan Liu, Jiahui Xu, Feng Jiang, Kuang Wang, Zefeng Zhao, Chu-Ren Huang, Jinghang Gu, Changqing Yin, Haizhou Li
arxiv-2602-23266.description: Abstract Achieving human-like responsiveness is a critical yet challenging goal for cascaded spoken dialogue systems. Conventional ASR–LLM–TTS pipelines follow a strictly sequential paradigm, requiring complete transcription and full reasoning before speech synthesis can begin, which results in high response latency. We propose the Discourse-Aware Dual-Track Streaming Response (DDTSR) framework, a low-latency architecture that enables listen-while-thinking and speak-while-thinking.

europmc-pmc5868293.creator: Ferreira RM, Pereira-Marques J, Pinto-Ribeiro I, Costa JL, Carneiro F, Machado JC, Figueiredo C.
europmc-pmc5868293.description: Objective Gastric carcinoma development is triggered by Helicobacter pylori . Chronic H. pylori infection leads to reduced acid secretion, which may allow the growth of a different gastric bacterial community. This change in the microbiome may increase aggression to the gastric

pmc-10574395.title: Zinc Oxide-Encapsulated Copper Nanowires for Stable Transparent Conductors
pmc-10574395.creator: Bo Wang, Shihui Yu, Liang Huang
pmc-10574395.description: Cu nanowire (NW)-based transparent conductors are considered to be highly promising constituents of next-generation flexible transparent electronics. However, the fast oxidation of copper under ambient conditions hinders the use of Cu NWs. Herein, we demonstrate a low-cost and scalable approach for preparing a ZnO shell on the surface of Cu NWs under ambient conditions.

pmc-10595097.title: Exposure to surrounding greenness and well-being in Portugal, a cross sectional study
pmc-10595097.creator: D S Resendes, M S Uva, P Morgado
pmc-10595097.description: BackgroundPositive mental health effects of nature have been studied before with relevant associations between the two easily found in literature. However, there is still a lack of population based studies that focus on the effect that the amount of surrounding greenness might have on well-being.

pmc-10726840.title: Subclinical epileptiform activity and sleep disturbances in Alzheimer's disease
pmc-10726840.creator: Astrid Devulder, Jaiver Macea, Alexandros Kalkanis, François‐Laurent De Winter, Mathieu Vandenbulcke, Rik Vandenberghe, Dries Testelmans, Maarten J A Van Den Bossche, Wim Van Paesschen
pmc-10726840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionSubclinical epileptiform activity (SEA) and sleep disturbances are frequent in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Both have an important relation to cognition and potential therapeutic implications. pmc-11343754.title: Anomalous continuum scattering and higher-order van Hove singularity in the strongly anisotropic S = 1/2 triangular lattice antiferromagnet
pmc-11343754.creator: Pyeongjae Park, E A Ghioldi, Andrew F May, James A Kolopus, Andrey A Podlesnyak, Stuart Calder, Joseph A M Paddison, A E Trumper, L O Manuel, Cristian D Batista, Matthew B Stone, Gábor B Halász, Andrew D Christianson
pmc-11343754.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The S = 1/2 triangular lattice antiferromagnet (TLAF) is a paradigmatic example of frustrated quantum magnetism. An ongoing challenge involves understanding the influence of exchange anisotropy on the collective behavior within such systems. Using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and advanced calculation techniques, we have studied the low and high-temperature spin dynamics of Ba2La2CoTe2O12 (BLCTO): a Co2+-based Jeff = 1/2 TLAF that exhibits 120° order below TN = 3.26 K.

pmc-11415796.title: Treatment of Bullous Pemphigoid with Avdoralimab: Multicenter, Randomized, Open-Labeled Phase 2 Study
pmc-11415796.creator: Thierry Passeron, Eric Fontas, Thierry Boye, Marie-Aleth Richard, Emmanuel Delaporte, Olivier Dereure
pmc-11415796.description: Rationale: Experimental data support the role for C5a–C5aR1 axis activation in bullous pemphigoid. We assessed the efficacy and safety of avdoralimab, a specific anti-C5aR1 mAb, for treating bullous pemphigoid. Methods: We conducted a phase 2 open-labeled randomized multicenter study. Patients with proven bullous pemphigoid were randomized (1:1) to receive superpotent topical steroids alone (group A) or with avdoralimab (group B).

pmc-11518086.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe ‘Lifelong Health’ framework of WHO emphasizes that investing in health during young ages fosters better health and higher quality of life in later years. When working with and for youth, using innovative and participatory approaches have become more important for effective health communication, especially in an era of increased environmental stimuli, digitalization, and decreased attention span for many young people, who are less attracted with traditional/ didactic health education and communication methods.ObjectivesThis paper aims to share practical experiences of a multidisciplinary

pmc-11576073.title: From Headache to Altered Consciousness: Headache Attributed to Hypoxia and/or Hypercapnia in a Smoker With Undiagnosed Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
pmc-11576073.creator: Tatsuya Tanaka, Nao Furusho, Hirotoshi Kawashima, Tadasu Okaya, Akira Matsuno
pmc-11576073.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We present the case of a 57-year-old male with a history of smoking, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and migraines who experienced a one-month history of dyspnea and headaches, followed by sudden-onset altered consciousness. Initial imaging ruled out cerebrovascular and infectious etiologies, and arterial blood gas analysis revealed severe hypercapnia and hypoxemia (partial pressure of arterial carbon dioxide: 117 mmHg, partial pressure of arterial oxygen: 111 mmHg under a 10 L/min oxygen mask).

pmc-11590033.title: Pirfenidone alleviates smoke inhalation lung injury of rats via the NF‐κB signaling pathway
pmc-11590033.creator: Tingting Lv, Kaiyuan Yang, Jinxiang Wang
pmc-11590033.description: ObjectiveSmoke inhalation lung injury (SILI) is a common complication in fires and wars, characterized by acute onset and severe condition. Pirfenidone (PFD), a new small‐molecule drug, has been shown to improve lung function and inhibit pulmonary fibrosis and inflammation. This study aimed to elucidate the effect and underlying mechanism of PFD on SILI in rats.

pmc-12821143.title: Drug intoxications in the emergency department: Our 1-year experience
pmc-12821143.creator: Ersoy Oksuz, Bilgehan Demir
pmc-12821143.description: OBJECTIVEDrug intoxication (DRI), which occurs due to accidental or suicidal use of high doses of drugs, has a high mortality and morbidity rate. emergency departments of hospitals are the units where these patients first come to the hospital, where the first interventions are performed and where the mortality rate is higher than other departments.

pmc-13096438.title: African inland wetland area on the rise during the 21st century
pmc-13096438.creator: Anzhen Li, Shengbo Chen, Kaishan Song, Yuanzhi Zhang, Zongming Wang, Dehua Mao
pmc-13096438.description: Wetlands face threats from climate change and human activities worldwide, yet the status of African wetlands remains unknown. This study mapped African wetlands and assessed area loss, drivers, and future trends under climate change using 270,000 sampling points, 810,000 Landsat images, and soil moisture data from 14 CMIP6 models.

pmc-13192208.title: Thyroid dysfunction and its association with micronutrients, lipids, and inflammation: an analytical case-control study
pmc-13192208.creator: Dilshad Hamad Mustafa, Kochr Ali Mahmood, Faisal Faruq Sadiq, Saman Taher Barzinjy, Dawan Jamal Hawezy, Sirwan Khalid Ahmed
pmc-13192208.description: BackgroundBiochemical, inflammatory, and immunological markers may provide insight into systemic alterations in individuals with or without thyroid dysfunction.AimThis study compared a comprehensive biomarker profile between adults without thyroid disease and those with thyroid dysfunction, and examined gender differences, correlations, and predictive markers.MethodsIn this case-control study, 120 adults without thyroid disease (cases) and 120 adults with thyroid dysfunction (controls) were enrolled.

pmc-13316314.title: Outcomes of mitral valve repair in ischemic mitral regurgitation: A two-decade experience
pmc-13316314.creator: Lokeswara Rao Sajja, Gopichand Mannam, Aditya Koppula, Satya Bhaskara Raju Dandu, Satyendranath Pathuri, Venkata Satya Siva Saikiran Krishnamurthy, V Ramachandra Raju Pusapati, Ramesh Gudapati, Jyothsna Guttikonda, Sriramulu Sompalli
pmc-13316314.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThe study objective was to evaluate long-term survival outcomes after mitral valve repair in patients with moderate or moderate-to-severe ischemic mitral regurgitation undergoing concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 212 consecutive patients who underwent mitral valve repair with restrictive annuloplasty and concomitant coronary artery bypass grafting for ischemic mitral regurgitation and coronary artery disease at a tertiary center between January 2005 and May 2025.

uslaw-usc-t26-s7524.title: 26 U.S.C. § 7524 — Annual notice of tax delinquency
uslaw-usc-t26-s7524.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s7524.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 77 (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Not less often than annually, the Secretary shall send a written notice to each taxpayer who has a tax delinquent account of the amount of the tax delinquency as of the date of the notice.
